content.value_statement: Feature changes can drift from intended product behavior when implementation begins before end-to-end specifications. This skill defines focused Momentic tests first and validates durable checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Identifies Momentic tests affected by a requested product change.
Creates or updates test specifications before modifying product code.
Follows nearby test conventions for modules, setup, actions, and assertions.
Plans deterministic test data and test-environment prerequisites.
Proposes the smallest affected test set at durable checkpoints.
Reports enabled tests, disabled tests, implemented behavior, and validation status.
limitations: Requires an existing repository with Momentic configuration or test conventions.
Does not execute Momentic tests without explicit user confirmation.
Does not guarantee test success when credentials, services, or environments are unavailable.
Relies on the installed momentic-test skill for detailed formats and MCP guidance.

use_cases.title: Specify a New User Journey
use_cases.description: Create a focused Momentic test that defines expected behavior before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Update Changed Product Behavior
use_cases.description: Revise existing Momentic coverage to express a changed contract without weakening unrelated assertions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reliable End-to-End Validation
use_cases.description: Define deterministic data, permissions, integrations, and test-only setup for a durable checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Affected Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature request and list each affected Momentic test path, its status, and the evidence for including it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before any test or product code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Write the Specification First
prompt_templates.prompt: Create or update the smallest Momentic test specification for this behavior. Preserve unrelated setup and explain any disabled state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the affected test set is known.

prompt_templates.title: Implement from the Test Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Momentic test diff as the product contract, then implement the feature and run appropriate fast repository checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after the test specification is on disk.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Durable Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Establish deterministic prerequisites, enable tests expected to pass, and propose the smallest Momentic run with expected cost and duration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a complete user-visible slice is ready.

output_examples.input: Add account deletion with a confirmation step.
output: Affected test: account-settings-delete, changed to specify confirmation and final account removal.
The specification is written before product code changes.
The test remains disabled until the deletion workflow and deterministic account setup are complete.

output_examples.input: Validate the completed search filter feature.
output: The existing search-filters test is enabled because the complete workflow is now available.
Required records and permissions are prepared through established test setup.
Proposed run: only search-filters, after explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Change a shared authentication module used by several tests.
output: Every consuming test is identified before the shared module changes.
Unrelated setup and assertions remain unchanged.
Fast checks run during implementation, while Momentic execution waits for a durable checkpoint.

best_practices: Treat the test diff as the product contract before implementation.
Reuse established modules and repository conventions for setup and known subflows.
Request confirmation before each Momentic run unless iterative reruns were explicitly authorized.
anti_patterns: Do not weaken assertions to match incomplete or incorrect implementation.
Do not hide reusable setup inside one large AI action goal.
Do not expose test setup capabilities in production or weaken production authorization.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests before product code?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires affected Momentic specifications to be on disk before product implementation begins.

faq.question: Will it run Momentic tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It proposes a specific run and waits for explicit confirmation because execution can consume time and credits.

faq.question: How does it choose affected tests?
faq.answer: It starts with named tests, traces shared behavior, and expands coverage only when repository evidence shows direct impact.

faq.question: Can a future test remain disabled?
faq.answer: Yes. The handoff must state why it is disabled and what condition allows it to be enabled.

faq.question: Does it support Momentic v1 tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs v1 changes through Momentic MCP tools instead of direct YAML editing.

faq.question: What validation runs during implementation?
faq.answer: It uses faster repository checks such as unit tests, type checking, and linting before proposing end-to-end execution.
